questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Being part norwegian, I wanted to better understand the norwegian culture, people and language, which is why I decided to choose Bergen. Specifically Bergen seemed to me an interesting place also because of the surrounding nature and the fact that I had heard good things about the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I had no issues

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much, it wasn't really needed

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Big recommendation of
hybel.no
, I made a profile detailing my situation and telling about myself, after which I got plenty of messages from people asking if I wanted to rent their apartment. Very easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is just as easy, if a bit more expensive, but if you feel reliant on the housing to make friends, go for that

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I made a profile, chose my courses, uploaded my passport and then that was pretty much it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure, I didn't get help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: All went well

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want to register for a course that doesn't seem open to exchange students, just write an email to the administration, the worst you can get is a no - it worked for me

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Both were second semester courses on BA level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I wouldn't say there was much of a difference, there is the same amount of lecture time compared to group work, etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Modern theatre history + performance analysis and theatre criticism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend both, but especially performance analysis and theatre criticism was a fun course, because it meant I also spent a lot of time exploring the theatre scene of Bergen seeing as it was necessary to the course

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food and alcohol is just a lot more expensive than in Denmark, so be prepared for that. I would also say budget for a second suitcase on the way home - you will be buying a lot of stuffl

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
More: food, alcohol, thrift shops
Less: coffee, public transportation

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different clubs, an orchestra, local gym for students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to Ad Fontes in HF Bygget and get free coffee, it's a very cute spot <33 And also get a Sammen gym membership right at the beginning, it's super inexpensive for five months

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Use DNT cabins! They are easy and cheap to book, and it is so fun to go on trips around Norway and hike in the nature surrounding the cabins. This is a must!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, especially considering the language similarity

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't do it much, but just show your interest, they will be polite and warm up to you soon enough

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: 17. maj, hiking culture, hotdog culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Take advantage of being so close to so much amazing nature, you'll never experience anything like it
2. Don't stress over finding friends, but engage yourself in social activities - my most meaningful relationships were with other danish students, so I also wouldn't shy away from pursuing activities with the other danes
3. You'll be fine academically, don't be scared of the academic level

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Can't think of anything

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The relationships I built with other people <33

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with the rainy weather - that is something you will have to get used to

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
